cues: Right front fender and bumper area appears crushed and pushed in against the lamp post, with the wheel arch deformed and the front wheel seemingly turned out; the area is partly hidden behind the door and tape, so the extent is uncertain.

damage_summary: The right front corner of the car appears crushed against a lamp post, with the fender and wheel area deformed. The rear and right side panels visible look intact.

lines.driver: replace right fender (severity 3): body 1.5-4.0 h, refinish 2.5-4.5 h at $68/h, parts $200-1500 x class multiplier 1.6-1.6

caveats: Stand-in table, not real pricing: every value marked 'assumption' is a placeholder pending real estimating data (CCC / Mitchell / Audatex).

Bounds, not calibrated intervals: low and high are the table's plausible bounds for the visible damage. They are not a statistical confidence interval, and how often real costs fall inside them has not been measured.
Hidden damage: only visible damage is priced. The high end includes an uplift when any item needs replacement, but structural, mechanical and underbody damage are not priced.
Parts type: the low end assumes aftermarket or repaired parts; the high end assumes OEM parts.
Region: labor uses the configured region tier; real body shop rates vary a lot by state.

Missing cost drivers, not included: ADAS sensor recalibration, paint blending into adjacent panels, taxes, rental and towing, storage, sublet work, and EV-specific work (battery inspection, high-voltage safety procedures).
cost.assumption_notice: Stand-in pricing table: every number is an assumption, not real estimating data. Not a payout amount.

reasons: Replacement-level damage reported with low confidence (right fender).
Estimated range reaches $4,000, above the $2,500 fast-track limit.
The cost range is wide (high is 6.0x the low), so the estimate is too uncertain to automate.
notes: Better photos of the right fender would help: 1 of 1 findings are low confidence.

boundary_notice: Triage aid only. This system never decides coverage, liability, denial or payment. A human adjuster reviews anything uncertain.
